item.title: An organ transplant controversy tests 'the dead donor rule'
item.description: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.

item.description: The regular news roundup with NPR's science podcast Short Wave covers a possible use for AI in emergency rooms, a distant planet and the link between cybersecurity and Daylight Saving Time.

item.title: Scientists think they've found ancient remnants of dinosaur blood
item.description: Scientists have studied plenty of dinosaur bones, eggs and footprints. Now, some think they've found their strongest evidence yet of dinosaur blood.

item.title: Mice can learn to fight by watching tiny rodent cage matches, study finds
item.description: Brain scientists set up "gladiator style" cage matches for mice — and found that simply observing fighting matches can rewire a mouse's brain to resemble those who actually fought.

item.title: How octopuses squeeze through teeny tiny holes
item.description: Robots used during search and rescue operations need to be able to wriggle through narrow cracks and crevices. Researchers have turned to a natural contortionist for inspiration — the octopus.

item.title: Oyster stocks have plunged in the Chesapeake. This resident wants to bring them back
item.description: Oyster reefs once abounded in the Chesapeake, but overharvesting slashed their populations, leading to poorer water quality and less habitat for other species. Now, researchers and local residents are finding creative ways to bring their numbers back up.
